sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days. Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds. It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review , saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6 , eh? This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity? If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

sources.title: How to complete the Frog side quest in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: The Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors need five songs played to them in OoT, which unlocks a new minigame. The Frogs in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time are found in the Zora River, and need songs played to them to complete their side quest. Referring to themselves as the Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors, Link's goal is to play five songs to them that they want to hear, which then unlocks a new minigame that you can play. If you can complete the frog song minigame, that then grants you a new piece of heart, a very valuable commodity. If you want to know how to complete this side quest, I'll take you through a full walkthrough below and what you need to know about the frogs and their love of music. To find the Five Froggish Tenors and start this side quest, you need to go to Zora River, which is accessed via the Northeast edge of Hyrule Field. Halfway along this route, on the North side, you'll find a small alcove with five pillars in it. This is where the Frogs are waiting. Simply interact with them like any NPC to begin the quest. You need to play several specific songs for the Frogs on your Ocarina for the chance to unlock the minigame, each one of which grants the players rupees as a reward. You need to play the following songs (in any order): As a bonus, players can also play the Song of Storms, learned from the Kakariko Windmill as an adult as part of a quest to learn the Lenses of Truth in Zelda Ocarina of Time . This isn't necessary to unlock the quest, but playing the Song of Storms for the frogs will grant you an additional piece of heart. Once all five necessary songs have been played, you can unlock the Frog Song minigame. Unfortunately, OoT doesn't actually explain how to control it, which can make it tricky. Here's how it works: Input it correctly, and you'll be awarded another piece of heart! After the first time, you'll be rewarded 5 Rupees for each successful attempt. This technically makes the Frog minigame a viable (if slow) means of infinitely farming money, especially if you're good at it. sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling way more physical copies than digital in Japan
sources.text: Roughly two-thirds of its sales were physical The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling more physical copies and digital copies in Japan, and by some margin to boot. Japanese magazine Famitsu 's latest sales chart numbers are in, with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time unsurprisingly at the top. According to its data, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Nintendo Switch 2 sold 537,041 physical copies at Japanese retailers. Earlier this week, Nintendo confirmed that the latest Zelda release had sold over 5.2 million copies within four days of launch, making it "the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days." Nintendo specified that 810,000 of these copies were sold in Japan. This means the Ocarina of Time remake sold around 272,959 digital copies in the region, roughly a third of the game's total sales in the region. With Sony 's decision to end physical disc production in 2028, and Rockstar releasing a ton of copies of GTA 6 today that feature nothing more than a code in a box that will activate in a week's time, there's been a lot of debate around physical game releases as of late. However, it's clear there's still a market out there for them, even if it is shrinking. Granted, Zelda's fortunes may have been helped by the fancy physical boxed copy that the game launched with, but even so, two-thirds of the game's sales in the region are certainly significant. Check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review . sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins four Golden Joystick Awards, including Ultimate and Console GOTY
sources.text: Capcom receives seven awards, including Studio of the Year and recognition for Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took place last night, with Resident Evil Requiem winning four awards including Ultimate Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year. The ninth instalment in the franchise also received Best Game Trailer, in addition to Angela Sant'Albano winning Best Lead Performer for her role as Grace Ashcroft. Capcom received seven awards, including Studio of the Year, Best Audio Design for Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Best Supporting Performer for Grace Saif’s role as Diana in Pragmata. AdHoc's Dispatch earned Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack. Meccha Chameleon was recognised as Best Indie Game (self-published), Best Multiplayer Game, Streamer’s Choice, and Developer’s Choice. Elsewhere, Remedy received Best Visual Design for Control Resonant, Unknown Worlds' Subnautica 2 won Best Early Access Game, Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert was named PC Game of the Year, and House House's Big Walk received Critics' Choice. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Crimson Desert wins 'PC Game of the Year' at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem and Meccha Chameleon were the night's other big winners. There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards, which are put on by PC Gamer's publisher. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. Yet that name, the Golden Joystick Awards , remains. Frankly, I'm glad about that. A little bit of reliability in this world is good for everyone. Which leads me to the point: The 44 th annual Golden Joystick Awards has now concluded, and the top gong , as my UK compatriots like to say for some reason—the Ultimate Game of the Year award, for the rest of us—has gone to Resident Evil Requiem , Capcom's latest tale of zombie-fueled bad news. Can't really argue with that call: PC Gamer's Elie Gould gave Resident Evil Requiem a whopping 92% score in their review , saying it "feels like you're playing a highlight reel of the best moments in the series." Requiem claimed three other wins on the night: Console Game of the Year, Best Game Trailer, and Best Lead Performer for Angela Sant'Albano's turn as Grace Ashcroft. Crimson Desert won for PC Game of the Year, which surprises me a bit given that it's also on consoles and pretty much the same experience. We liked that one too: Not quite as enthusiastically, but it still earned an enviable 80% review score . "Vast and obtuse in a way that is going to frustrate some and exhilarate others," as reviewer Mollie Taylor put it: "A fascinating journey, even when the destination isn't all that." Multiplayer hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon was the night's other big winner, taking home four awards for Best Multiplayer Game, Best Indie Game (self-published), the Steamers' Choice Award, and Developer's Choice Award. Dispatch won twice, for Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack, and The Witcher also sort of claimed two wins as well: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered took the trophy for Best Remake/Remaster, while The Witcher 4 won for Most Wanted Game. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. So there you have it, 44 years down and hopefully many more to come—all of them bearing that glorious golden name. Here's your full list of 2026 Golden Joystick Awards winners: 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem actor after Golden Joystick Awards win: "Capcom, you cannot fail!"
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem walked away with the biggest prize of the night at the Golden Joystick Awards yesterday, capping off a total of four wins with the prestigious title of Ultimate Game of the Year. But in an acceptance speech delivered on-stage by Leon Kennedy actor Nick Apostoledes, there was an allusion to an even bigger winner - Capcom itself. "What can I say?" Apostoledes began. "Resident Evil going 30 years strong this year - how fitting is it to win Ultimate Game of the Year for Requiem? We are just honored to be part of a project that is so beloved, a franchise that is so beloved. Thank you to the fans, thank you for keeping this alive. Capcom, you cannot fail." Apostoledes' remarks were followed up by pre-recorded comments from Requiem director Koshi Nakanishi, who said he was "thrilled" to accept the award, and spoke about how encouraging it was for a single-player game to win, especially in such a crowded field. While Resi itself will be making the big headlines, however, Apostoledes touched on an interesting point: the legendary run that Capcom itself is on. As well as claiming two GOTY titles for Requiem, that title also secured wins in the Best Game Trailer category, and a Best Lead Performer win for Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano. But two of Capcom's other titles - Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword - were also in contention for several categories, each one claiming its own win. Onimusha took the prize for Best Audio Design, while Diana actress Grace Saif took home Best Supporting Performer for her role in Pragmata. With three out of its four major releases this year claiming wins, perhaps it was of little surprise that Capcom would also take home the prize for Studio of the Year. 2026 has been a jewel in a crown that Capcom has been polishing for some time now. In the last four years, it's been on an excellent run. The last time a new release has slipped below a MetaCritic score of 80 was 2023's Exoprimal, and the closest thing it's had to a flop was Monster Hunter Wilds, which was plagued by performance issues. Elsewhere, it's been turning Resident Evil back into an essential release, breathing new life into classics, and successfully bringing life to new IP. It's been a relatively slow, quiet process, but Capcom has rarely put a foot wrong since 2020, and the community is starting to take note. 2027 looks like a quieter year for the studio, but with Resident Evil Veronica on the horizon, it looks like fans will still be eating pretty well. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit. sources.text: Nintendo has announced its Black Friday 2026 deals, which include $50 in savings on a “ Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” and select games at $20-off the suggested retail price. Starting November 22 through December 5, rev up for Black Friday with the “Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” featuring a Nintendo Switch 2 system, a full download of the Mario Kart World game and a three-month (90-day) Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership for the suggested retail price of $499.99, a savings of $50. Plus, from November 22 through November 29, select games for Nintendo Switch 2 like Donkey Kong Bananza and Nintendo Switch games such as Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 will be $20-off the suggested retail price. All offers available while supplies last. In addition to select retailers, these promotions will be available at the Nintendo New York and Nintendo San Francisco stores. The “Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” promotion will also be available on the Nintendo Store website. The Nintendo New York and Nintendo San Francisco stores will feature festive window displays and seasonal decor and are a one-stop destination for holiday shopping for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch, plus games, gifts, exclusive items, and more. Share the joy of Nintendo this holiday with exclusive products, collectibles and apparel inspired by your favorite characters and games including Mario , The Legend of Zelda , Animal Crossing , Pikmin , and Splatoon . Holiday gift guides, festive shopping bags, and, for a limited time, a gift with purchase (requires minimum spend) will be available while supplies last. Holiday shoppers looking to get an early jump on enjoying some games can also check out a sale on Nintendo eShop and the Nintendo Store beginning November 19 through December 2.

sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Its Black Friday Sale Plans, With Its Own Games Getting Rare $20 Discounts
sources.text: Black Friday 2026 Nintendo Nintendo Switch 2 Nintendo discounts its in-house games about as often as it warmly encourages downloading ROMs, so it’s something of a big deal to see the announcement that come November 22, games like Donkey Kong Bananza ,Â Metroid Prime 4 , andÂ Kirby Air Riders will all be discounted by $20. The Thanksgiving season will also see the return of theÂ Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle on November 22, priced at $500, which is the current price of a Switch 2 on its own. You may well remember that when the Switch 2 launched in June 2025, the version bundled with a download code forÂ Mario Kart World was then priced at $500. But in the 18 months since, the price of the Switch 2 has jumped up $50 thanks to the AI-driven component crisis and Trump’s inane tariffs. Thus, returning to the baseline represents something of a bargain in our upside-down times. That bundled deal, which also comes with three months of Nintendo Switch Online, will run from November 22 to December 5, and obviously depends on available stock. For a slightly shorter window, a handful of Nintendo’s own games will also get the Black Friday treatment via retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, GameStop and Walmart, as well as Nintendo’s own U.S. stores. From November 22 to 29, Switch 2 titles Donkey Kong Bananza ,Â Metroid Prime 4: Beyond , Kirby Air Riders , andÂ Super Mario Party Jamboree will all be $20 less, meaning the very splendid Donkey Kong game will be just $50 instead of $70. Meanwhile the Switch versions ofÂ Super Mario Party Jamboree andÂ Metroid Prime 4Â will also receive twenty-buck reductions. Running over yet another set of dates (Nintendo never wants anything to be straightforward), the eShop will be having its own Black Friday sale, this time from November 19 to December 2. So far there are no details about which games will be seeing price drops, but hopefully it’ll see the same titles getting similar discounts. But this is Nintendo, so who knows? Clearly the eShop’s sale will also encompass every other publisher’s games at lower prices too. (Presumably at this point Ubisoft will be paying us to get a copy of Mario vs. Rabbids .) Seeing Nintendo’s own games getting price cuts is not common, especially ones as recent asÂ DK Bananza andÂ Metroid Prime 4 , so if you were waiting on either, this’ll be the time to pounce. sources.title: 25 Original XBOX Games Available Today on PC via XBOX Backward Compatibility
sources.text: Today, 21 more original XBOX games are coming to PC, bringing the XBOX Backward Compatibility on PC library to 25 games as we celebrate 25 years of XBOX. We’re also introducing achievements for four original XBOX games, with more titles planned over time. We brought the first four original XBOX games to PC earlier this year, including handhelds such as the ROG XBOX Ally family, for the first time. Today, there are more familiar favorites to revisit, and more classics to discover. We’ve also improved performance and stability for the first four games and every game now supports mouse and keyboard too The 21 additional games available to players in supported countries starting today are: These join the four games already available on PC: We are going to bring even more original XBOX games to PC in the future. Starting today, we’re introducing one of the top requested features from the XBOX community. For the first time ever, players can now earn achievements in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords, BLiNX: The Time Sweeper , and Conker: Live and Reloaded . The addition of achievements also apply when you play these games on XBOX One and XBOX Series consoles. Make sure to take the latest system update so you can start earning them. In some cases, achievements may unlock based on progress you’ve already made. We worked closely with each game’s developers and publishers as we designed the achievements to make sure they fit the spirit of each title. We plan to bring achievements to more original XBOX games over time. The games you’ve played are part of your history with XBOX. Bringing more of them to PC and adding achievements are a few ways we’re ensuring you can continue to play the games you love, wherever you may choose. Requires Windows 11. Specific features vary by game; download required (xbox.com/game-compatibility). Select markets only. Game purchase or Game Pass subscription may be required.

sources.title: 21 original Xbox games are now on PC via backward compatibility
sources.text: There are now 25 classic Xbox games available on PC, and four have achievements Xbox has added 21 new original Xbox games to its backwards compatibility catalogue on PC. The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind, Star Wars Battlefront, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, TimeSplitters 2, and more have been added to the catalogue, bringing the roster up to 25 on PC . Four of the games available on the service will also have unlockable achievements. The following games will join the PC backward compatibility catalogue with achievements:Â Star Wars: KOTOR, Star Wars: KOTOR 2, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, and Conker: Live and Reloaded. You can unlock achievements for these games when playing on an Xbox console too. This announcement comes as part of Xbox’s ongoing FanFest. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also used the event to reveal that id Software is working on its next game after Doom: The Dark Ages . Xbox will also be hoping that this earns it some goodwill in the gaming community, following a year full of layoffs . These layoffs are part of Xbox’s ongoing “reset”, which has seen multiple studios spun off, sold, or merged with others, such as Bethesda and Obsidian , who now work together. Others have seen a massively reduced headcount.

stories.summary: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored: that Wolfenstein 3 is in development.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed to Be in Development at MachineGames
sources.text: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames confirmed what had long been rumored : that Wolfenstein 3 is in development. MachineGames will once again be developing it. Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus was released to rave reviews in 2017, but MachineGames then put the series on hold to develop 2024's absolutely stellar Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. But now, Wolfenstein is back on the front burner at the Swedish studio. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at Machine Games," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed on X. "One of gaming’s most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh MachineGames added on to Sharma's post, which shows a page of the Wolfenstein 3 script, saying simply , "His reputation precedes him," referring to the action described on the script page. "Wolfenstein 3 is in production." The developers also confirmed that actors Brian Bloom (as B.J. Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (as Grace Walker) will return via a photo of the pair in the developer's motion-capture studio. Wolfenstein 3 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Last year, in an interview with Noclip , MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson said the team had "always seen [BJ's story] as a trilogy," adding: "That journey for BJ, even during those first weeks at [id Software], when we mapped out New Order — we still had the plan for at least [BJ], what would happen in the second one and what would happen in the third one. "I think that's important to say, because⁠ — at least, I hope ⁠— we're not done with Wolfenstein yet. We have a story to tell." That's not all that Wolfenstein fans have to look forward to, as the pioneering first-person shooter series is also being developed into a TV series at Amazon. Xbox's official 25th anniversary is this Sunday, November 15. Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Wolfenstein 3 is in the works at MachineGames, Xbox CEO announces
sources.text: Asha Sharma says MachineGames "has done remarkable work" on Wolfenstein Wolfenstein 3 is officially in the works at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced. Sharma has been firing off semi-big announcements via her official Twitter account all day in celebration of Xbox's 25th anniversary, including confirmation that Id Software is working on a new game, but this is undoubtedly the biggest news of the bunch. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames," reads a tweet from Sharma. "One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." Not much else was revealed about the Wolfenstein revival, but it's exciting to know it's a full-blown mainline entry and not a spinoff ala Young Blood (which I enjoyed, to be fair). This will be the first mainline entry in the legendary first-person shooter series since 2017's Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus, which somehow was almost 10 years ago. Remember when I said "not much else was revealed" about Wolfenstein 3? Well, that's because Sharma was generous enough to tease us with a picture appearing to show the first page of Wolfenstein 3's dialogue script, seemingly confirming the first chapter is called Nazitraz. The scene opens in the inside of an interrogation cell with a conversation between longtime Wolfenstein protagonist William Joseph "B.J." Blazkowicz and a German-speaking character called Otto, which could be a number of bad guys throughout Wolfenstein history. B.J.'s longtime right hand, Fergus, also seems to be in the scene, but that's about everything that can be inferred based on what's shown. MachineGames has been Bethesda's trusted Wolfenstein developer since 2014, starting with Wolfenstein: The New Order. No details regarding platforms or release timing were revealed. sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Wolfenstein 3 Officially Confirmed by XBOX CEO Asha Sharma
sources.text: Asha Sharma, XBOX CEO, has officially confirmed that MachineGames is producing Wolfenstein 3. Sharma announced the news on social media, calling Wolfenstein one of gaming’s most important franchises and saying she can’t wait to share more. The post she shared on Twitter featured a small portion of the script’s first chapter. The first chapter is entitled “Nazitraz.” MachineGames hasn’t been shy about their desire to finish the Wolfenstein trilogy. In February, a casting call revealed plot details, reportedly centering on a character named Sofiya. She’s described as an 8- to 11-year-old Ukrainian orphan who bonds with William Blazkowicz, the franchise’s main protagonist. The young character is also said to be traumatized by war, which makes her suspicious, but she’s ultimately described as a strong survivor. That casting call noted that performance capture was scheduled to begin in April, with shooting extending into 2027. Also in February, MachineGames studio director Jerk Gustaffson noted that the studio, which had been making Wolfenstein games since 2014, intended to finish the trilogy. “We wanted to finish the trilogy. When we do that, that is something that I don’t want to comment on. It can be now, it can be later, but we’re not done with it. That’s what I can say,” he said at the time. For now, there’s no hint of a release window for MachineGames’ next Wolfenstein game. Insider Gaming will continue to monitor the story and report any updates as more information becomes available. sources.title: Wolfenstein 3 is in production at MachineGames
sources.text: Earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed on Twitter that she'd seen The Elder Scrolls 6. Now, she's announcing that MachineGames is making Wolfenstein 3 with a photo of the script attached to a tweet. I don't miss E3, but it feels like a step down in terms of spectacle to go from on-stage trailer reveals to an executive just tweeting it out. MachineGames followed up a few minutes later with their own tweet , saying, "His reputation precedes him. Wolfenstein 3 is in production." As well as the same photo of the script, they attached a photo of Debra Wilson (who played Resistance cell leader Grace Walker in The New Colossus) recording motion-capture. It's been a couple of years since Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, though MachineGames did release a Quake expansion for its 30th anniversary in the meantime. A page of script and a photo of a motion-capture session doesn't tell us much about how far along it is, but I wouldn't expect it super soon. It'd be nice to have something to tie into the upcoming Wolfenstein TV series coming from the same folks as the Fallout show . What do we think they'll subtitle Wolfenstein 3? sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: The Outer Worlds 2’s first DLC arrives December 2
sources.text: The first in a two-part Side Effects Guaranteed narrative adventure arrives soon, with part two coming spring 2027. The time has come to expand on the experience for The Outer Worlds 2 with the first of a two-part story expansion, Side Effects Guaranteed, arriving on December 2. After a distress signal from a derelict ship is picked up, you and your crew quickly get embroiled into the story of an abandoned settlement, a power struggle for the future of the Sub Rosa criminal organization, and the fate of a team who has been subjected to something that will cause them all to die from explosive cell death. Really, it’s more a liquefaction than explosion, but it means death nonetheless. A brand new story filled with moral quandaries and consequences big and small isn’t the only thing you’ll experience in the first DLC. An Earth Directorate Commander should always be sure to have a weapon at their side, and there are five new weapons to add to the arsenal. Such as the Immobilizer. Think of it like a gun that makes gravity forget to exist around its target, allowing them to float in the air, so you can switch to another weapon and pick them off as you like. Great for combining with grenades for anti-gravity explosions or the Tactical Time Dilation device for slowing down time and getting some critical shots in. There is also the 1/6 Resolver that allows every sixth bullet that is fired from it to pack an extra special punch. For those who built their characters just right, they won’t have to empty the gun every time to get that critical hit, either. Other weapons include a weapon that does additional damage to creatures, a special Tossball Stick, and a new plasma weapon for some energy fun. Yet it isn’t all about the weapons. Side Effects Guaranteed will also bring with it a level cap increase up to 36, new perks, new flaws, and a new Sub Rosa radio station with 20 new songs. There is also the all-new region of Elysium Valley to explore with unique quests and new facilities to make your way through. That’s a lot of new! While the events of the DLC do trigger right before the point of no return in the main game, there is also a way to jump easily into the action. From the main menu if you start a new game, you will see an option to start Side Effects Guaranteed directly. This will load a pre-made character at level 27 that you can assign skill points and perks to so you can experience the DLC however you’d like and get started right away. Not happy with the character you made (or the one you already have)? Coming to everyone at the same time as the release of Side Effects Guaranteed is a new update that will allow players to respec their character at any time. And for those who want more skills to play around with, a new addition to the custom game options allows you to adjust how many skill points you get per level. Find the balance that is right for you. Or become an Earth Director demi-god. Your worlds, your way. But remember, however you decide to deal with Sub Rosa or the subjects of Elysium Valley will have consequences. Side effects, some might say, that will lead directly into the next installment of The Outer Worlds 2 two-part story expansion when it releases in the spring of 2027. Until then, may skill catch you where fortune fails. Side Effects Guaranteed releases on December 2nd or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Efeitos colaterais estão garantidos no primeiro DLC de The Outer Worlds 2, que chega em 2 de dezembro
sources.text: Um sinal de socorro leva você e sua tripulação da Incognito até uma nave abandonada, onde vocês encontram os tripulantes em animação suspensa. Tudo indica que há algo de errado, especialmente a poça do que muito provavelmente já foi uma pessoa. Você recupera uma mensagem em vídeo deixada pela capitã da nave, que explica que a tripulação foi contaminada por algo durante um roubo e que, se não encontrarem uma cura, isso causará uma morte celular explosiva. E, por morte celular explosiva, ela quer dizer algo mais parecido com uma… “liquefação”. Pelo jeito da poça no chão: é liquefação mesmo. Esse é o cenário para o lançamento da primeira parte de uma expansão narrativa em DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , dividida em duas partes, em 2 de dezembro. Em Side Effects Guaranteed, a mensagem em vídeo que você encontrou leva até Gordon Hazen, um dos principais agentes da Sub Rosa, uma organização criminosa formada por pessoas que compartilham dos mesmos ideais e escolheram viver roubando das diversas facções em vez de trabalhar para elas. Gordon, por sua vez, envia você para Elysium Valley, uma nova região de Eden que abriga um assentamento de antigos súditos do Protetorado, esquecidos por seus líderes. Ele acredita que eles podem ter as respostas para salvar sua tripulação. Embora prefira a diplomacia à violência, ele precisa que você faça o que for necessário para conseguir as informações de que precisa. Mas Gordon não é o único interessado em Elysium Valley. Outro agente da Sub Rosa, Algernon Lankester, quer recrutar você para ajudá-lo a explorar os súditos em benefício próprio. O destino dos súditos, dos agentes congelados da Sub Rosa e o futuro da própria organização estão nas suas mãos, nosso intrépido Comandante. No entanto, uma nova história não será a única novidade de Side Effects Guaranteed quando o DLC for lançado daqui a algumas semanas. Além de explorar a nova região de Elysium Valley, os jogadores vão encontrar novas ameaças, como canídeos ferozes e sprats primitivos. O que é um sprat primitivo? É só um sprat normal, mas cerca de 100 vezes maior. Com certeza, eles são tão amigáveis quanto seus primos bem menores e vão perdoar todas as vezes em que você atirou neles “sem querer” enquanto explorava Arcadia. Com essas novas ameaças, vem a possibilidade de deixar seu Comandante ainda mais forte e, é claro, com mais defeitos (mas no bom sentido). O limite de nível aumentará de 30 para 36, trazendo mais pontos de habilidade para diversificar sua configuração de personagem. Poder chegar ao nível 36 também significa que você poderá adquirir mais três vantagens, com 15 vantagens inéditas adicionadas às opções disponíveis. Também serão introduzidos quatro novos defeitos que podem mudar a forma de jogar com seu Comandante, como “Lethally Tolerant”, que reconhece sua resistência acumulada a substâncias químicas e aumenta sua toxicidade máxima. Isso é ótimo na hora, mas, se você sofrer um colapso de toxicidade, morrerá instantaneamente. Outro exemplo é “Must Have Been the Wind”, que marca um “alvo de assassinato” em um grupo de combate. Eliminar o alvo concede um bônus de 20% no dano e na velocidade até o fim do combate, mas não conseguir eliminá-lo ou atacar alguém que não seja o alvo aplica ao jogador uma penalidade de 10% no dano e na velocidade por 30 segundos. São recompensas que realmente vêm acompanhadas de grandes riscos. Side Effects Guaranteed também trará novas armas, novas armaduras e novos trajes para cada um dos companheiros, além de uma estação de rádio inédita comandada pela Sub Rosa, com 20 novas músicas para o jogo. Para quem quiser ir direto à ação no DLC, será adicionado um novo ponto de partida alternativo ao menu principal ao selecionar um novo jogo, permitindo começar com um arquivo de jogo salvo personalizado que coloca você no início do DLC. Inicie o jogo, distribua seus pontos de habilidade e de vantagem e aproveite Side Effects Guaranteed sem demora! Essa aventura repleta de conteúdo, com uma história profunda e sistemas para criar seu Comandante ideal, preparará o terreno para o próximo DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , que chegará no segundo trimestre de 2027. As escolhas que você fizer terão impacto direto no próximo DLC. A primeira parte dessa história que se desenrola ao longo da expansão, Side Effects Guaranteed, será lançada em 2 de dezembro e também está incluída na Edição Premium ou no Upgrade para a Edição Premium de The Outer Worlds 2 .
